description: DraftForge structured-log dashboard. Overview row at the top summarizes inventory, log rate, warn/error rate, and top error events. Each system in the canonical taxonomy gets its own collapsed row below — expand the one you care about. Bottom row surfaces lines that fail `| json` parsing so we can fix them at source. See .claude/skills/logging/SKILL.md for the taxonomy.

panels.description: Every (system, subsystem) tuple seen in range. Surfaces newly-shipped subsystems and silently-dropped ones.

targets.expr: sum by (system, subsystem) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment="$env"} | json | __error__="" | system!="" [$__range]))

panels.title: Subsystem inventory

panels.description: Most frequent warn/error events. Top of this list is where to spend the next round of fixes.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (event, system, subsystem) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment="$env"} | json | __error__="" | level=~"warning|error" [$__range])))

panels.title: Top error messages

panels.description: Total log rate aggregated by system.

targets.expr: sum by (system) (rate({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment="$env"} | json | __error__="" | system!="" [$__interval]))

panels.description: Log lines that Loki's `| json` parser rejects. Source labels (code_file_path, code_function_name, code_line_number) tell you which Python file is emitting broken JSON — usually an f-string containing a stray `{` like a dict literal or repr() output. Fix at source by switching the call to structlog kwargs.

targets.expr: {service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment="$env"} | json | __error__="jsonparsererr"

panels.title: Lines that broke `| json` (jsonparsererr)

panels.description: Which source files are emitting broken JSON, ranked by count. Fix the top entries at source.

targets.expr: topk(20, sum by (code_file_path, code_function_name, code_line_number) (count_over_time({service_name=~"$service", deployment_environment="$env"} | json | __error__="jsonparsererr" [$__range])))
